title.zh: 卷二百〇三 列傳第九十: 方技 工藝
title.en: Volume 203 Biographies 90: Medicine and Divination, Arts and Crafts
title.raw: 卷二百〇三 列傳第九十: 方技 工藝 Volume 203 Biographies 90: Medicine and Divination, Arts and Crafts

sentences.zh: 自昔帝王勃興，雖星曆醫卜方術異能之士，莫不過絕於人，類非後來所及，蓋天運也。

translations.literal: From antiquity, whenever emperors and kings rose vigorously, even those skilled in astronomy, medicine, divination, alchemy, and other exceptional arts surpassed ordinary humanity, seeming beyond what later generations could reach—it was the operation of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times, whenever dynasties arose, specialists in astronomy, medicine, divination, and the occult arts invariably stood far above ordinary people, as though later ages could never match them—surely this reflected Heaven's design.

sentences.zh: 元有中土，巨公異人，身兼數器者，皆應期而出，相與立法創制，開物成務，以輔成大業，亦云盛哉。

translations.literal: When the Yuan held the Central Plain, great lords and extraordinary men who combined many skills all emerged in accord with the times, together establishing laws and creating institutions, opening things and completing tasks, to assist in accomplishing the great enterprise—truly magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan in China, eminent figures and prodigies mastering several disciplines appeared right on cue, jointly framing laws and institutions and advancing practical undertakings to support the founding enterprise—a remarkable flourishing indeed.

sentences.zh: 若道流釋子，所挾多方，事適逢時，既皆別為之傳。

translations.literal: As for Daoist clerics and Buddhist monks, whose holdings were many-sided, as matters happened to coincide with the times, each has already received a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist adepts and Buddhist clergy, with their varied pursuits, have each been given separate biographies when their careers aligned with the times.

sentences.zh: 其他以術數言事輒驗，及以醫著效，被光寵者甚眾。

translations.literal: Others who by numerology and divination spoke of affairs and were invariably validated, and those who by medicine achieved notable effect—those showered with honor were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Many others won favor through prognostication that proved true or medicine that yielded striking cures.

sentences.zh: 舊史多闕弗錄，今取其事蹟可見者，為《方技篇》。

translations.literal: Old histories mostly omitted and did not record them; now selecting those whose deeds remain visible, this forms the Treatise on Arts and Skills.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories often left them out; here we gather figures whose careers can still be traced into this Treatise on Arts and Skills.

sentences.zh: 而以工藝貴顯，亦附見焉。

translations.literal: And those who by craftsmanship rose to noble eminence are also appended herein.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen who rose to high rank are included as well.

sentences.zh: 田忠良，字正卿，其先平陽趙城人，金亡，徙中山。

translations.literal: Tian Zhongliang, courtesy name Zhengqing, his ancestors were men of Zhaocheng in Pingyang; when Jin perished, the family moved to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhongliang (Zhengqing), originally from Zhaocheng in Pingyang, moved to Zhongshan after the fall of the Jin.

sentences.zh: 忠良好學，通儒家、雜家言。

translations.literal: Zhongliang loved learning and mastered the teachings of the Confucian and Miscellaneous schools.
translations.idiomatic: He was studious and versed in both Confucian and eclectic learning.

sentences.zh: 嘗識太保劉秉忠於微時。

translations.literal: He once knew Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong in his humble early days.
translations.idiomatic: He had known Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong before Liu rose to power.

sentences.zh: 秉忠薦於世祖，遣使召至，帝視其狀貌步趨，顧謂侍臣曰：「是雖以陰陽家進，必將為國用。

translations.literal: Bingzhong recommended him to Shizu; envoys were sent to summon him; the emperor observed his appearance and gait, turned and said to attending ministers: "Although this one advances as a Yin-Yang specialist, he will surely be put to state use."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhong recommended him to Kublai, who summoned him; observing his bearing, the emperor told his attendants, "Though he comes as a cosmologist, he will surely serve the state."

sentences.zh: 」俄指西序第二人謂忠良曰： 「彼手中握何物？

translations.literal: Shortly he pointed to the second man on the western side and said to Zhongliang: "What does that man hold in his hand?"
translations.idiomatic: Then he pointed to the second man on his right and asked Zhongliang, "What is he holding?"

sentences.zh: 」忠良對曰：「雞卵也。

translations.literal: Zhongliang replied: "A chicken egg."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang answered, "A hen's egg."

sentences.zh: 」果然。

translations.literal: It was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: It was exactly so.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，又曰：「朕有事縈心，汝試占之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and again said: "I have a matter troubling my heart; try divining it."
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor said, "Something weighs on my mind—divine it."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「以臣術推之，當是一名僧病耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "By my art I deduce it should be illness of a certain monk."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "By my art, it is illness afflicting a certain monk."

sentences.zh: 「帝曰：「然，國師也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is—the Imperial Preceptor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yes—the Imperial Preceptor."

sentences.zh: 」遂遣左侍儀奉御也先乃送忠良司天台，給筆札，令秉忠試星曆、遁甲諸書。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Ye Xianai to escort Zhongliang to the Directorate of Astronomy, provided brush and paper, and ordered Bingzhong to test him in books on stars, calendars, and war-board divination.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ye Xianai to escort Zhongliang to the Directorate of Astronomy with writing materials and had Liu Bingzhong examine him in astronomy, calendrics, and divination manuals.

sentences.zh: 秉忠奏曰：「所試皆通，司天諸生鮮有及者。

translations.literal: Bingzhong memorialized: "In all tested he is thoroughly versed; among astronomy students few can match him."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhong reported that he passed every examination and few among the directorate's students could equal him.

sentences.zh: 」詔官之司天。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him to office in the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him to the directorate.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕用兵江南，困於襄樊，累年不決，奈何？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I use troops in Jiangnan, bogged down at Xiang and Fan, unresolved for many years—what to do?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Our campaign in the south has stalled at Xiangyang and Fancheng for years—what will break the impasse?"

sentences.zh: 」忠良對曰：「在酉年矣。」

translations.literal: Zhongliang replied: "In the year of you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang answered, "In the year of the Rooster."

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，阿里海牙奏請率十萬眾渡江，朝議難之，帝密問曰：「汝試筮之，濟否？

translations.literal: In the 11th year of Zhiyuan, Alihaia memorialized requesting to lead one hundred thousand across the river; court deliberation found it difficult; the emperor secretly asked: "Try divining—will it succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: In 1274, Alihaia proposed crossing the Yangtze with a hundred thousand men; when court opinion wavered, the emperor privately asked whether divination favored success.

sentences.zh: 」忠良對曰：「濟。

translations.literal: Zhongliang replied: "It will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang said it would succeed.

sentences.zh: 」帝獵於柳林，禦幄殿，侍臣甚眾，顧忠良曰：「今拜一大將取江南，朕心已定，果何人耶？

translations.literal: The emperor hunted at Willow Grove, in the imperial tent-palace, attendants very numerous; he turned to Zhongliang and said: "Now I appoint a great general to take Jiangnan; my mind is already settled—who is it in truth?"
translations.idiomatic: While hunting at Willow Grove from his tent amid a large entourage, he asked Zhongliang whom he had in mind to conquer the south.

sentences.zh: 」忠良環視左右，目一人，對曰：「是偉丈夫，可屬大事。

translations.literal: Zhongliang looked all around, eyed one man, and replied: "That is a majestic man—great affairs may be entrusted to him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang scanned the company, fixed on one man, and said, "That formidable figure can bear the command."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「此伯顏也，為西王旭烈兀使，朕以其才留用之，汝識朕心。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said: "This is Bayan—envoy of the Western Prince Hulagu; I kept him for his talent; you know my mind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed, "That is Bayan—Hulagu's envoy, whom I kept for his talent. You read my thoughts."

sentences.zh: 」賜鈔五百貫、衣一襲。

translations.literal: He bestowed five hundred strings of paper money and one suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with five hundred strings of paper money and a suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 七月十五日夜，白氣貫三台，帝問何祥，忠良對曰：「三公其死乎！

translations.literal: On the night of the fifteenth day of the seventh month, white vapor pierced the Three Platforms; the emperor asked what omen it was; Zhongliang replied: "Will the Three Dukes die!"
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the fifteenth of the seventh month, a white vapour crossed the Three Platforms asterism; asked its meaning, Zhongliang said, "Surely the Three Dukes will die!"

sentences.zh: 」未幾，太保劉秉忠卒。

translations.literal: Before long, Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Liu Bingzhong died.

sentences.zh: 八月，帝出獵，駐輦召忠良曰：「朕有所遺，汝知何物，還可復得否？

translations.literal: In the eighth month the emperor went out hunting, halted the imperial carriage and summoned Zhongliang, saying: "I have lost something—do you know what it is, and whether it can be recovered?"
translations.idiomatic: During the August hunt he summoned Zhongliang and asked what he had lost and whether it could be found.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「其數珠乎？

translations.literal: He replied: "Is it your prayer beads?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked if it was the emperor's prayer beads.

sentences.zh: 明日，二十里外人當有得而來獻者。

translations.literal: Tomorrow someone twenty li away will find them and come to present them.
translations.idiomatic: He said someone twenty li away would find them and bring them in the morning.

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: And so it indeed proved.
translations.idiomatic: It happened exactly as he said.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，賜以貂裘。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and bestowed a sable fur coat.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased, the emperor gave him a sable coat.

sentences.zh: 十月，有旨問忠良：「南征將士能渡江否？

translations.literal: In the tenth month there was an edict asking Zhongliang: "Can the southern-expedition troops cross the river?"
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was asked whether the southern army could cross the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 勞師費財，朕甚憂之。

translations.literal: Wearying the army and spending wealth—I am greatly worried.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added that the strain on men and treasure worried him deeply.

sentences.zh: 」忠良奏曰：「明年正月當奏捷矣。」

translations.literal: Zhongliang memorialized: "In the first month of next year victory reports should be presented."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang said victory dispatches would arrive in the first month of the coming year.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，師取鄂州，丞相伯顏遣使來獻宋寶，有玉香爐，輟以賜忠良，及金織文十匹。

translations.literal: In the first month of the 12th year, the army took Ezhou; Chancellor Bayan sent envoys to present Song treasures; there was a jade incense burner, which was set aside to bestow on Zhongliang, along with ten bolts of gold brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In January 1275 the army captured Ezhou; Bayan sent Song booty including a jade incense burner for Zhongliang and ten bolts of gold brocade.

sentences.zh: 二月，帝不豫，召忠良謂曰：「或言朕今歲不嘉，汝術云何？

translations.literal: In the second month the emperor was unwell; he summoned Zhongliang and said: "Some say this year is inauspicious for me—what does your art say?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill in the second month, he asked whether the year boded ill for him.

sentences.zh: 」忠良對曰：「聖體行自安矣。

translations.literal: Zhongliang replied: "Your sacred person will soon be at ease of itself."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang assured him his health would soon mend.

sentences.zh: 」三月，帝疾愈，賜銀五百兩、衣材三十匹。

translations.literal: In the third month the emperor's illness abated; he bestowed five hundred taels of silver and thirty bolts of garment material.
translations.idiomatic: By the third month he had recovered and rewarded Zhongliang with five hundred taels of silver and thirty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 五月，車駕清暑上都，遣使來召曰：「叛者浸入山陵，久而不去，汝與和禮霍孫率眾往視之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the imperial carriage summered at Shangdu; envoys were sent summoning him: "Rebels have entered the mountain mausoleum and long do not leave—you and Hoelqüsun lead troops to go inspect."
translations.idiomatic: While summering at Shangdu in May, the emperor sent for him and Hoelqüsun to investigate rebels lingering at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 」既至，山陵如故，俄而叛兵大至，圍之三匝，三日不解。

translations.literal: When they arrived the mausoleum was as before; soon rebel troops arrived in force, surrounding them thrice deep, three days without relief.
translations.idiomatic: The tombs seemed undisturbed, but rebels soon surrounded them three deep for three days.

sentences.zh: 忠良引眾夜歸，敵殊不覺，和禮霍孫以為神，白其事於帝，賜黃金十兩。

translations.literal: Zhongliang led the crowd back by night; the enemy utterly did not notice; Hoelqüsun regarded it as miraculous, reported the affair to the emperor, and Zhongliang was bestowed ten taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang slipped away by night without the enemy noticing; Hoelqüsun reported the marvel to the emperor, who gave Zhongliang ten taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 八月，以海都為邊患，遣皇子北平王那木罕、丞相安童征之，忠良奏曰：「不吉，將有叛者。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, because Haidu was a border peril, the Prince of Peiping Naiman and Chancellor Antong were sent to campaign; Zhongliang memorialized: "Inauspicious—there will be rebels."
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Naiman and Chancellor Antong were dispatched against Haidu in the eighth month, Zhongliang warned of mutiny.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offence.

sentences.zh: 十二月，諸王昔里吉劫皇子、丞相以入海都，帝召忠良曰：「朕幾信讒言罪汝，今如汝言，汝祀神致禱，雖黃金朕所不吝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the prince Shiregi seized the prince and chancellor to go over to Haidu; the emperor summoned Zhongliang: "I nearly believed slander and punished you; now it is as you said—sacrifice to the spirits and pray; though it be gold I will not be sparing."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Prince Shiregi seized the heir and Antong for Haidu; the emperor told Zhongliang he had nearly punished him on false charges and offered gold for prayers.

sentences.zh: 」忠良對曰：「無事於神，皇子未年當還。

translations.literal: Zhongliang replied: "No need for dealings with spirits—the prince, not yet of age, should return."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang said no prayers were needed—the young prince would return before year's end.

sentences.zh: 」後果然。

translations.literal: Later it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: And so it proved.

sentences.zh: 十四年八月，車駕駐隆興北，忠良奏曰：「昔里吉之叛，以安童之食不彼及也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the 14th year, the imperial carriage halted north of Longxing; Zhongliang memorialized: "Shiregi's rebellion—because Antong's provisions did not reach him."
translations.idiomatic: At Longxing in the eighth month of 1277 he explained Shiregi's revolt as stemming from short rations under Antong.

sentences.zh: 今宿衛之士，日食一瓜，豈能充飢，竊有怨言矣。

translations.literal: Now the palace-guard soldiers eat one melon a day—how can that fill hunger? Secretly there are resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that guards fed only one melon a day were grumbling.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，笞主膳二人，俾均其食。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, flogged the two heads of commissariat, and ordered equal distribution of food.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the commissary officers beaten and rations equalized.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，汴梁河清三百里，帝曰：「憲宗生，河清；

translations.literal: In the third month of the 15th year the Bianliang River ran clear for three hundred li; the emperor said: "When Xianzong was born, the river ran clear;
translations.idiomatic: When the Bian River ran clear for three hundred li in 1278, the emperor noted it had cleared at Möngke's and his own births.

sentences.zh: 朕生，河又清；

translations.literal: When I was born, the river again ran clear;
translations.idiomatic: When I was born, it cleared again;

sentences.zh: 今河又清，何耶？

translations.literal: now the river again runs clear—why?
translations.idiomatic: He asked why it cleared again.

sentences.zh: 」忠良對曰：「應在皇太子宮矣。

translations.literal: Zhongliang replied: "It should correspond to the Heir Apparent's palace."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang said it foretold events in the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 」帝語符寶郎董文忠曰：「是不妄言，殆有徵也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Seal Keeper Dong Wenzhong: "This is not reckless speech—likely there is a portent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Dong Wenzhong that this was no idle prophecy.

sentences.zh: 十八年，特命為太常丞。

translations.literal: In the 18th year he was specially appointed Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 he was appointed Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 少府為諸王昌童建宅於太廟南，忠良往僕其柱，少府奏之，帝問忠良，對曰：「太廟前豈諸王建宅所耶？

translations.literal: The Palace Store built a residence for Prince Changtong south of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Zhongliang went to attend the pillars; the Palace Store memorialized; the emperor asked Zhongliang, who replied: "Before the Imperial Temple—is that where princes build houses?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Palace Store built Prince Changtong a house south of the temple, Zhongliang objected that princes should not build before the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 」又奏曰：「太廟前無馳道，非禮也。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "Before the Imperial Temple there is no imperial roadway—this is not ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged opening a ceremonial avenue before the temple.

sentences.zh: 」即敕中書辟道。

translations.literal: Immediately an edict ordered the Secretariat to open the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was ordered to clear the road at once.

sentences.zh: 國製，十月上吉，有事於太廟。

translations.literal: By national regulation, on the upper auspicious day of the tenth month there are affairs at the Imperial Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan custom held ancestral rites on the auspicious day of the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 或請牲不用牛，忠良奏曰：「梁武帝用面為犧牲，後如何耶？

translations.literal: Some requested sacrificial victims without using cattle; Zhongliang memorialized: "Liang Wudi used dough as sacrificial victim—how did it turn out afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed dough instead of cattle, he cited Liang Wudi's failed dough sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Director of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Director.

sentences.zh: 二十年，將徵日本國，召忠良擇日出師，忠良奏曰：「僻陋海隅，何足勞天戈。

translations.literal: In the 20th year, about to campaign against Japan, the emperor summoned Zhongliang to choose the day for launching the army; Zhongliang memorialized: "A remote shabby corner of the sea—what worth to weary Heaven's weapons?"
translations.idiomatic: When invasion of Japan was planned in 1283, he urged that the distant isles did not warrant imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored him.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，請建太社於朝右，建郊壇於國南。

translations.literal: In the 24th year he requested building the Grand Altar of Earth on the right of the court, and the suburban altar on the south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1287 he had the Grand Earth Altar built east of court and the suburban altar south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄兼引進使。

translations.literal: Soon he additionally held the post of Reception Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also served as Reception Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: In the 29th year he was transferred to Director of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1292 he became Director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，遷昭文館大學士、中奉大夫，兼太常太卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he was transferred to Grand Academician of the Hall for the Glorification of Culture, Middle Maintainer of the Faith, and concurrently Grand Director of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1297 he became Grand Academician of the Hall for the Glorification of Culture, Middle Maintainer of the Faith, and concurrent Grand Director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十一年，成宗崩，阿忽台等持異謀，將以皇后教，祔成宗於廟。

translations.literal: In the 11th year Chengzong died; Ahutai and others held divergent plots, intending to follow the empress's command to enshrine Chengzong in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died in 1307, Ahutai's faction planned to enshrine him by empress's decree rather than proper rite.

sentences.zh: 忠良爭曰：「嗣皇帝祔先帝於廟，禮也；

translations.literal: Zhongliang contended: "For the succeeding emperor to enshrine the preceding emperor in the temple is ritual propriety;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang insisted that only the reigning emperor could install his predecessor—

sentences.zh: 皇后教，非制也。

translations.literal: an empress's command is not regulation.
translations.idiomatic: an empress's order was irregular.

sentences.zh: 」阿忽台等怒曰：「制自天降耶？

translations.literal: Ahutai and others angrily said: "Does regulation descend from Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Ahutai snapped that ritual did not fall from heaven.

sentences.zh: 汝不畏死，敢沮大事！

translations.literal: You do not fear death—you dare obstruct the great affair!
translations.idiomatic: They threatened him for blocking their plan.

sentences.zh: 」忠良竟不從。

translations.literal: Zhongliang ultimately did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 既而仁宗以太弟奉皇太后至自懷州，潛與密謀誅阿忽台等。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter Renzong as Heir Apparent escorted the Empress Dowager back from Huaizhou and secretly joined in plotting to execute Ahutai and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong then arrived from Huaizhou with the empress dowager and plotted Ahutai's downfall.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，進榮祿大夫、大司徒，賜銀印。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, Zhongliang was advanced to Grand Honored Physician, Grand Minister of Education, and bestowed a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong promoted him to Grand Honored Physician and Grand Minister of Education with a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，又進光祿大夫，領太常禮儀院事。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, he was further advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and put in charge of the Directorate of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong further made him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and head of the ritual directorate.

sentences.zh: 延祐四年正月卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Yanyou he died, age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in January 1317 at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠守正佐運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封趙國公，諡忠獻。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted the title Meritous Subject Who Pushed Loyalty, Upheld Rectitude, and Assisted the Dynasty; Grand Preceptor; Opening the Government with Equal Ceremony to the Three Ducal Ministers; Senior Pillar of State; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao; temple name Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Duke of Zhao with the temple name Loyal Presentation and the highest ministerial honors.

sentences.zh: 子天澤，翰林侍講學士、嘉議大夫、知制誥兼修國史。

translations.literal: His son Tian Ze was Hanlin Attendant Academic Expositor, Grand Master of Kind Counsel, and Drafting Proclamations with concurrent editing of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tian Ze served as Hanlin expositor, drafting edicts and editing the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 靳德進，其先潞州人，後徙大名。

translations.literal: Jin Dejin—his ancestors were men of Luzhou, later moved to Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Dejin's family came from Luzhou and later moved to Daming.

sentences.zh: 祖璇，業儒。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuan practiced Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan was a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 父祥，師事陵川郝溫，兼善星曆。

translations.literal: His father Xiang studied under Hao Wen of Lingchuan and was also skilled in stars and calendars.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiang studied under Hao Wen of Lingchuan and mastered astronomy.

sentences.zh: 金末兵亂，與母相失，母悲泣而盲，祥訪得之，舐其目，百日復明，人稱其孝。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin there was military chaos; he lost his mother; his mother wept in grief and went blind; Xiang searched and found her, licked her eyes, and in a hundred days sight returned—people praised his filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin collapse he found his blind mother after searching and restored her sight by licking her eyes—an act famed as filial piety.

sentences.zh: 國初，玉出乾劉敏行省於燕，辟祥置幕下，佩以金符。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty, Liu Min served as Branch Secretariat in Yan; he recruited Xiang to set beneath his tent curtain and wore him with a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty Liu Min of Yan recruited him and issued a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 時籓帥得擅生殺，無辜者多賴祥以免。

translations.literal: At that time feudatory commanders could arbitrarily kill or spare life; many innocents relied on Xiang to escape execution.
translations.idiomatic: Many innocents owed their lives to his intercession with commanders who held arbitrary power of life and death.

sentences.zh: 贈集賢大學士，諡安靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents; temple name Anjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents with the name Peaceful Rest.

sentences.zh: 德進為人材辨，幼讀書，能通大義，父歿，益自刻勵，尤精於星曆之學。

translations.literal: Dejin was intelligent and discerning in talent; in youth he read books and could penetrate great principles; when his father died he redoubled self-discipline and was especially accomplished in the learning of stars and calendars.
translations.idiomatic: Dejin was bright and well read; after his father's death he applied himself especially to astronomy.

sentences.zh: 世祖命太保秉忠選太史官屬，德進以選授天文、星曆、卜筮三科管勾，凡交蝕躔次、六氣侵沴，所言休咎輒應。

translations.literal: Shizu ordered Grand Preceptor Bingzhong to select Astronomical Directorate staff; Dejin by selection was appointed supervisor of the three sections of astronomy, star-calendars, and divination; concerning eclipses, planetary positions, and the six qi invading and clashing—whatever he spoke of fortune and calamity was invariably validated.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhong selected him for the directorate's three bureaus; his predictions of eclipses, planetary motion, and seasonal qi invariably proved true.

sentences.zh: 時因天象以進規諫，多所裨益。

translations.literal: At the time he used celestial phenomena to advance remonstrance and admonition, benefiting much.
translations.idiomatic: He often admonished the emperor by citing heaven's signs to good effect.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書監，掌司天事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Palace Library, managing affairs of the Directorate of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Palace Library in charge of astronomy.

sentences.zh: 從征叛王乃顏，揆度日時，率中機會。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against the rebel prince Nayan, he calculated and estimated days and times, generally hitting the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Prince Nayan his timing calculations usually proved exact.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲剿絕其黨，德進獨陳天道好生，請緩師以待其降。

translations.literal: The generals wished to exterminate root and branch his faction; Dejin alone expounded Heaven's Way loving life, requesting to slow the army to await their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When generals wanted to annihilate Nayan's followers, he alone urged mercy and a pause for surrender.

sentences.zh: 俄奏言：「叛始由惑於妖言，遂謀不軌，宜括天下術士，設陰陽教官，使訓學者，仍歲貢有成者一人。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized: "The rebellion began from being deluded by demonic speech, thereafter plotting irregular conduct—it is fitting to round up the empire's occult specialists, establish Yin-Yang instruction officials, have them train learners, and each year present one who has achieved success."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed registering occultists empire-wide, appointing Yin-Yang instructors, training students, and presenting one graduate annually—

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，遂著為令。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this and thereupon codified it as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: which the emperor enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 張康，字汝安，號明遠，潭州湘潭人。

translations.literal: Zhang Kang, courtesy name Ruan, style name Mingyuan, a man of Xiangtan in Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kang (Ruan, style Mingyuan) was from Xiangtan in Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖安厚，父世英。

translations.literal: His grandfather Anhou, father Shiying.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Anhou and his father Shiying.

sentences.zh: 康早孤力學，旁通術數。

translations.literal: Kang was orphaned early and studied diligently, broadly mastering numerology and divination.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he studied hard and mastered divination and related arts.

sentences.zh: 宋呂文德、江万裡、留夢炎皆推重之，辟置幕下。

translations.literal: Under Song, Lü Wende, Jiang Wanli, and Liu Mengyan all esteemed him and recruited him to their staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Song ministers Lü Wende, Jiang Wanli, and Liu Mengyan all valued him and placed him on their staffs.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，隱衡山。

translations.literal: When Song perished, he hid on Mount Heng.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song fell he withdrew to Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，世祖遣中丞崔彧祀南嶽，就訪隱逸。

translations.literal: In the 14th year of Zhiyuan, Shizu sent Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu to sacrifice at the Southern Marchmount and on the way seek out recluses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 Kublai sent Vice Censor Cui Yu to sacrifice at the Southern Marchmount and seek out recluses.

sentences.zh: 彧兄湖南行省參政崔斌言康隱衡山，學通天文地理。

translations.literal: Yu’s elder brother, Branch Secretariat Participant Cui Bin of Hunan, said Kang was hidden on Mount Heng and his learning penetrated astronomy and geography.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yu’s brother Bin, a Hunan Secretariat official, reported that Kang lived on Mount Heng and was versed in astronomy and geography.

sentences.zh: 彧還，具以聞，遣使召康，與斌偕至京師。

translations.literal: When Yu returned he reported fully; envoys were sent to summon Kang, who came to the capital together with Bin.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Cui Yu reported to the throne; Kang was summoned and arrived at the capital with Bin.

sentences.zh: 十五年夏四月，至上都見帝，親試所學，大驗，授著作佐郎，仍以內嬪松夫人妻之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the 15th year he went to Shangdu to see the emperor; the emperor personally tested his learning—it greatly proved true; he was appointed Assistant Compiler and also given the inner consort Lady Song as wife.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1278 he met the emperor at Shangdu, passed a personal examination of his arts, was appointed Assistant Compiler, and was given the inner consort Lady Song in marriage.

sentences.zh: 凡召對，禮遇殊厚，呼以明遠而不名。

translations.literal: Whenever summoned for audience, courtesy was exceptionally thick; he was called Mingyuan and not by name.
translations.idiomatic: At every audience he was treated with exceptional honor and addressed by his style Mingyuan rather than his name.

sentences.zh: 嘗面諭：凡有所問，使極言之。

translations.literal: The emperor once instructed him face to face: whenever anything was asked, let him speak to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told him to speak freely on any matter he was asked about.

sentences.zh: 十八年，康上奏：「歲壬午，太一理艮宮，主大將客、參將囚，直符治事，正屬燕分。

translations.literal: In the 18th year Kang memorialized: "In the year renwu, Great One governs the Gen palace; it governs the great general as guest and the participating general as prisoner; the straight talisman handles affairs—this directly belongs to the Yan region."
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 he memorialized that in the year renwu the Great One star governed the Gen palace, placing the great general as guest and the participating general as prisoner, with the straight talisman in charge—an omen for the Yan region.

sentences.zh: 明年春，京城當有盜兵，事干將相。

translations.literal: Next spring the capital should have bandit-soldiers; the affair will involve generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He predicted banditry in the capital the following spring involving generals and ministers.

sentences.zh: 」十九年三月，盜果起京師，殺阿合馬等。

translations.literal: In the third month of the 19th year bandits indeed rose in the capital and killed Ahmad and others.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1282 rebels struck the capital and killed Ahmad and others, as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 帝欲徵日本，命康以太一推之，康奏曰：「南國甫定，民力未蘇，且今年太一無算，舉兵不利。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to campaign against Japan and ordered Kang to calculate by Great One; Kang memorialized: "The southern states have just been settled and the people’s strength is not yet restored; moreover this year Great One has no reckoning—raising troops is unfavorable."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned to invade Japan, Kang urged that the south had only just been pacified, the people were not yet restored, and the year’s Great One calculations forbade war.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 嘗賜太史院錢，分千貫以與康，不受，眾服其廉。

translations.literal: Once the Astronomical Directorate’s funds were bestowed; a thousand strings were divided to give Kang, but he did not accept—everyone admired his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When a thousand strings from the directorate’s funds were offered him, he refused, and all admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 久之，乞歸田裡，優詔不許，遷奉直大夫、秘書監丞。

translations.literal: After a long time he begged to return to his fields; a gracious edict did not permit it; he was transferred to Grand Master for Attending to Governance and Vice Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He later begged to retire to his home village but was refused and promoted to Grand Master for Attending to Governance and Vice Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 年六十五卒。

translations.literal: At age sixty-five he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 子天祐。

translations.literal: His son was Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Tianyou.

sentences.zh: 李杲，字明之，鎮人也，世以貲雄鄉里。

translations.literal: Li Gao, courtesy name Mingzhi, was a man of Zhen; his family for generations was wealthy and powerful in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao (Mingzhi) of Zhen came from a family that had long been wealthy and powerful locally.

sentences.zh: 杲幼歲好醫藥，時易人張元素以醫名燕趙間，杲捐千金從之學，不數年，盡傳其業。

translations.literal: Gao in his youth loved medicine and pharmacy; at the time the Yidao man Zhang Yuansu was famed for medicine between Yan and Zhao; Gao donated a thousand gold to study under him; in not many years he fully transmitted his craft.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved medicine; he paid a thousand in gold to study under Zhang Yuansu, the famed physician of Yan and Zhao, and within a few years mastered his art.

sentences.zh: 家既富厚，無事於技，操有餘以自重，人不敢以醫名之。

translations.literal: His family being already rich and thick, he had no need for the craft as occupation; holding surplus he made himself weighty—people did not dare address him by the name of physician.
translations.idiomatic: His family was already wealthy, so he did not practice medicine for a living and carried himself with such weight that people hesitated to call him a mere physician.

sentences.zh: 大夫士或病其資性高謇，少所降屈，非危急之疾，不敢謁也。

translations.literal: Great officers and gentlemen, if ill, found his nature lofty and sparing in yielding—unless the illness was critically urgent, they did not dare call on him.
translations.idiomatic: Officials found him proud and reluctant to defer; unless the case was dire they did not dare summon him.

sentences.zh: 其學於傷寒、癰疽、眼目病為尤長。

translations.literal: His learning in cold-damage disorders, abscesses and sores, and eye diseases was especially outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially renowned for cold-damage disorders, abscesses, and eye diseases.

sentences.zh: 北京人王善甫，為京兆酒官，病小便不利，目睛凸出，腹脹如鼓，膝以上堅硬欲裂，飲食且不下，甘淡滲洩之藥皆不效。

translations.literal: The Beijinger Wang Shanfu, wine officer of Jingzhao, was ill with difficult urination, eyeballs protruding, belly swollen like a drum, knees upward hard and seeming about to split, food and drink nearly not going down—sweet bland percolating-draining medicines all ineffective.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shanfu, Jingzhao wine officer, suffered obstructed urination, bulging eyes, a drum-tight belly, and knees so rigid they seemed about to split; sweet bland diuretics failed, and he could scarcely eat.

sentences.zh: 杲謂眾醫曰：「疾深矣。

translations.literal: Gao told the crowd of physicians: "The illness is deep."
translations.idiomatic: Gao told the other physicians that the case was grave.

sentences.zh: 《內經》有之：膀胱者，津液之府，必氣化乃出焉。

translations.literal: The Inner Canon has it: the bladder is the storehouse of fluids—only when qi transforms can they exit.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the Inner Canon: the bladder is the storehouse of fluids, and only when qi transforms can they be discharged.

sentences.zh: 今用滲洩之劑而病益甚者，是氣不化也。

translations.literal: Now using percolating-draining agents while the illness grows worse means qi is not transforming.
translations.idiomatic: The worsening under diuretics showed that qi was not transforming.

sentences.zh: 啟玄子云：'無陽者陰無以生，無陰者陽無以化。

translations.literal: Master Qixuan said: "Without yang, yin has nothing to generate; without yin, yang has nothing to transform."
translations.idiomatic: He quoted Wang Bing: without yang yin cannot generate, and without yin yang cannot transform.

sentences.zh: '甘淡滲洩皆陽藥，獨陽無陰，其欲化得乎？

translations.literal: Sweet bland percolating-draining are all yang medicines—with yang alone and no yin, how can transformation be achieved?
translations.idiomatic: Sweet bland diuretics are yang drugs; with yang alone and no yin, how could transformation occur?

sentences.zh: 」明日，以群陰之劑投，不再服而愈。

translations.literal: The next day he administered agents of the yin group; without taking again the patient recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he gave yin-natured medicines, and the patient recovered without further doses.

sentences.zh: 西台掾蕭君瑞，二月中病傷寒發熱，醫以白虎湯投之，病者面黑如墨，本證不復見，脈沉細，小便不禁。

translations.literal: Western Terrace clerk Xiao Junrui in the second month fell ill with cold-damage fever; physicians administered White Tiger Decoction; the patient’s face turned black as ink, the original syndrome no longer visible, pulse deep and fine, urination uncontrolled.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Xiao Junrui took cold damage in the second month; physicians gave White Tiger Decoction, turning his face black as ink, hiding the original syndrome, with a deep fine pulse and incontinence.

sentences.zh: 杲初不知用何藥，及診之，曰：「此立夏前誤用白虎湯之過。

translations.literal: Gao at first did not know what medicine had been used; when he examined he said: "This is the error of using White Tiger Decoction before the Start of Summer."
translations.idiomatic: Gao at first did not know what had been given; on examination he said White Tiger Decoction had been wrongly used before summer.

sentences.zh: 白虎湯大寒，非行經之藥，止能寒腑藏，不善用之，則傷寒本病隱曲於經絡之間。

translations.literal: White Tiger Decoction is extremely cold—not a channel-traveling medicine; it can only chill the bowels and viscera; used poorly, the cold-damage root illness hides curled within the channels and network.
translations.idiomatic: White Tiger is intensely cold, not a channel-traveling drug; misused it chills the viscera and drives the root illness into the channels.

sentences.zh: 或更以大熱之藥救之，以苦陰邪，則他證必起，非所以救白虎也。

translations.literal: If one then uses great heat medicines to rescue it, to bitter the yin evil, other syndromes will certainly arise—not the way to save from White Tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Rescuing with great heat to bitter the yin evil would only provoke other syndromes—not the way to undo White Tiger harm.

sentences.zh: 有溫藥之昇陽行經者，吾用之。

translations.literal: There are warming medicines that uplift yang and travel the channels—I will use them.
translations.idiomatic: He would use warming medicines that uplift yang and travel the channels.

sentences.zh: 」有難者曰： 「白虎大寒，非大熱何以救，君之治奈何？

translations.literal: A doubter said: "White Tiger is great cold—without great heat how to save it? What is your treatment?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone objected that great cold required great heat to counter it and asked his method.

sentences.zh: 」杲曰：「病隱於經絡間，陽不升則經不行，經行而本證見矣。

translations.literal: Gao said: "The illness hides in the channels; if yang does not rise the channels do not move; when the channels move the root syndrome appears."
translations.idiomatic: Gao replied that the disease lay hidden in the channels and that once yang rose and the channels moved, the root syndrome would reappear.

sentences.zh: 本證又何難焉。

translations.literal: Once the root syndrome appears, what difficulty is there?
translations.idiomatic: Then treating the root syndrome would be straightforward.

sentences.zh: 」果如其言而愈。

translations.literal: It indeed followed his words and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: It happened exactly as he said, and the patient recovered.

sentences.zh: 魏邦彥之妻，目翳暴生，從下而上，其色綠，腫痛不可忍。

translations.literal: The wife of Wei Bangyan—cataract suddenly arose from below upward, its color green, swelling and pain unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bangyan’s wife developed a cataract rising from below, green in color, with unbearable swelling and pain.

sentences.zh: 杲云：「翳從下而上，病從陽明來也。

translations.literal: Gao said: "Cataract from below upward—illness comes from Yangming."
translations.idiomatic: Gao said a cataract rising from below indicated Yangming involvement.

sentences.zh: 綠非五色之正，殆肺與腎合而為病邪。

translations.literal: Green is not among the five colors as orthodox—perhaps lung and kidney combine to form the illness.
translations.idiomatic: Green was not a standard color of the five phases, suggesting combined lung and kidney pathology.

sentences.zh: 」乃瀉肺腎之邪，而以入陽明之藥為之使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he purged evil from lung and kidney and used medicines entering Yangming as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: He purged lung and kidney evil and used Yangming-entering medicines as envoys.

sentences.zh: 既效矣，而他日病復作者三，其所從來之經，與翳色各異。

translations.literal: It was effective, but another day the illness recurred three times; the channel from which it came and the cataract color each differed.
translations.idiomatic: It worked, but the disease recurred three times, each time from a different channel with a different color.

sentences.zh: 乃曰：「諸脈皆屬於目，脈病則目從之。

translations.literal: He then said: "All channels belong to the eyes; when channels are ill the eyes follow."
translations.idiomatic: He then said all channels belong to the eyes, and channel disease affects the eyes.

sentences.zh: 此必經絡不調，經不調，則目病未已也。

translations.literal: This must be that the channels and network are not regulated; if channels are not regulated, eye illness is not yet ended.
translations.idiomatic: The channels were not regulated, so the eye disease had not ended.

sentences.zh: 」問之果然，因如所論而治之，疾遂不作。

translations.literal: On inquiry it was indeed so; he treated according to this reasoning and the illness thereafter did not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiry confirmed it; he treated accordingly and the disease did not return.

sentences.zh: 馮叔獻之侄櫟，年十五六，病傷寒，目赤而頓渴，脈七八至，醫欲以承氣湯下之，已煮藥，而杲適從外來，馮告之故。

translations.literal: Feng Shuxian’s nephew Li, age fifteen or sixteen, fell ill with cold-damage; eyes red and suddenly thirsty; pulse seven or eight beats to the breath; physicians wished to purge with Order-the-Qi Decoction; the medicine was already brewing when Gao happened to come from outside and Feng told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shuxian’s nephew Li, about fifteen or sixteen, had cold damage with red eyes and sudden thirst and a pulse of seven or eight beats; physicians were brewing Order-the-Qi Decoction when Gao arrived.

sentences.zh: 杲切脈，大駭曰：「幾殺此兒。

translations.literal: Gao felt the pulse and was greatly alarmed: "You nearly killed this child."
translations.idiomatic: Gao felt the pulse and cried out that they had nearly killed the boy.

sentences.zh: 《內經》有言：'在脈，諸數為熱，諸遲為寒。

translations.literal: The Inner Canon says: in the pulse, all rapid counts as heat, all slow as cold.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the Inner Canon that rapid pulses indicate heat and slow pulses cold.

sentences.zh: '今脈八九至，是熱極也。

translations.literal: Now the pulse is eight or nine beats—this is extreme heat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet an eight- or nine-beat pulse indicated extreme heat.

sentences.zh: 而《會要大論》云：'病有脈從而病反者何也？

translations.literal: Yet the Great Treatise on Correspondences says: when illness has pulse following but illness contrary, what is it?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Great Treatise asks what it means when the pulse seems to follow the signs but the disease is contrary.

sentences.zh: 脈至而從，按之不鼓，諸陽皆然。

translations.literal: Pulse arrives and follows, but when pressed it does not throb—all yang is like this.
translations.idiomatic: When the pulse seems to follow but pressing shows no throbbing, all yang signs are thus.

sentences.zh: '此傳而為陰證矣。

translations.literal: This has transmitted and become a yin syndrome.
translations.idiomatic: The case had transmitted into a yin syndrome.

sentences.zh: 令持姜、附來，吾當以熱因寒用法處之。

translations.literal: Bring ginger and aconite—I will treat it by the method of using heat for cold.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered ginger and aconite and would treat by using heat for cold.

sentences.zh: 」藥未就而病者爪甲變，頓服者八​​兩，汗尋出而愈。

translations.literal: Before the medicine was ready the patient’s fingernails changed; he immediately took eight taels; sweat soon came out and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Before the decoction was ready the boy’s nails changed color; he took eight taels at once, sweated, and recovered.

sentences.zh: 陝帥郭巨濟病偏枯，二指著足底不能伸，杲以長針刺骫中，深至骨而不知痛，出血一二升，其色如墨，又且謬刺之。

translations.literal: Shaanxi commander Guo Juji was ill with hemiplegia; two fingers touched the sole of the foot and could not extend; Gao with a long needle pierced the center of the popliteal fossa, deep to the bone without knowing pain, bloodletting one or two sheng, the color like ink, and again needled erroneously.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Guo Juji had hemiplegia with two toes curled under the sole; Gao needled deep into the popliteal fossa to the bone without pain, letting one or two sheng of ink-dark blood, and needled again.

sentences.zh: 如此者六七，服藥三月，病良已。

translations.literal: Thus six or seven times; after taking medicine three months the illness was thoroughly cured.
translations.idiomatic: He did this six or seven times; after three months of medicine the patient was fully cured.

sentences.zh: 裴擇之妻病寒熱，月事不至者數年，已喘嗽矣。

translations.literal: The wife of Pei Ze was ill with cold and heat; menstruation had not come for several years; she was already coughing.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ze’s wife had alternating chills and fever, had not menstruated for years, and was already coughing.

sentences.zh: 醫者率以蛤蚧、桂、附之藥投之，杲曰：「不然，夫病陰為陽所搏，溫劑太過，故無益而反害。

translations.literal: Physicians all used gecko, cinnamon, and aconite medicines; Gao said: "Not so—the illness is yin struck by yang; warming agents are too extreme, therefore no benefit but rather harm."
translations.idiomatic: Physicians gave gecko, cinnamon, and aconite; Gao said yin struck by yang was harmed by excessive warming.

sentences.zh: 投以寒血之藥，則經行矣。

translations.literal: Administer cold-blood medicines and menstruation will flow.
translations.idiomatic: Cold-blood medicines would restore her menses.

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: Soon after it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: It proved so.

sentences.zh: 杲之設施多類此。

translations.literal: Gao’s applications were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Gao’s treatments were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 當時之人，皆以神醫目之。

translations.literal: People of the time all regarded him as a divine physician.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries regarded him as a divine physician.

sentences.zh: 所著書，今多傳於世云。

translations.literal: Books he authored now mostly circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His books still circulate widely.

sentences.zh: 孫威，渾源人。

translations.literal: Sun Wei, a man of Hunyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wei was from Hunyuan.

sentences.zh: 幼沉鷙，有巧思。

translations.literal: In youth deep and shrewd, with ingenious craft.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was shrewd and ingenious.

sentences.zh: 金貞祐間，應募為兵，以驍勇稱。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyou era of Jin he answered the recruitment as soldier and was styled valiant and brave.
translations.idiomatic: During Jin’s Zhenyou era he enlisted and won fame for valor.

sentences.zh: 及雲中來附，守帥表授義軍千戶，從軍攻潞州，破鳳翔，皆有功。

translations.literal: When he came from Yunzhong to submit, the defending commander memorialized appointing him commander of a righteous army of one thousand households; following the army he attacked Luzhou, broke Fengxiang, and all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Coming from Yunzhong to submit, he was made commander of a thousand-man righteous army and distinguished himself at Luzhou and Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 善為甲，嘗以意制蹄筋翎根鎧以獻，太祖親射之，不能徹，大悅。

translations.literal: He was skilled at making armor; once by his own idea he made armor of hoof sinew and tail-root feathers to present; Taizu personally shot it and could not penetrate—greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at armor-making and once presented armor of hoof sinew and feather roots that even Genghis Khan’s arrow could not pierce.

sentences.zh: 賜名也可兀蘭，佩以金符，授順天安平懷州河南平陽諸路工匠都總管。

translations.literal: He was granted the name Ke’ewulan, wore a gold tally, and was appointed Grand Director-General of Craftsmen for Shuntian, Anping, Huaizhou, Henan, Pingyang, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Ke’ewulan, given a gold tally, and made grand director-general of craftsmen across several circuits.

sentences.zh: 從攻邠、乾，突戰不避矢石，帝勞之曰：「汝縱不自愛，獨不為吾甲胄計乎！

translations.literal: Following attacks on Bin and Qian, in sudden battles he did not avoid arrows and stones; the emperor comforted him: "You may not love yourself, but will you not plan for my armor?"
translations.idiomatic: In assaults on Bin and Qian he braved arrows and stones; the emperor told him to think of his armor as well as his courage.

sentences.zh: 」因命諸將衣其甲者問曰：「汝等知所愛重否？

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the generals wearing his armor to be asked: "Do you know what is dearly valued?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked generals wearing Sun’s armor whether they knew what they valued.

sentences.zh: 」諸將對，皆失旨意。

translations.literal: The generals replied—all missed the emperor’s intent.
translations.idiomatic: Their answers all missed his point.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「能捍蔽爾輩以與我國家立功者，非威之甲耶！

translations.literal: Taizong said: "What can shield you to render merit for our state—is it not Wei’s armor?"
translations.idiomatic: Ögedei said it was Sun Wei’s armor that shielded them to serve the state.

sentences.zh: 而爾輩言不及此，何也？

translations.literal: Yet you speak without reaching this—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet they had not said so—why?

sentences.zh: 」復以錦衣賜威。

translations.literal: Again he bestowed brocade robes on Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He again gave Sun Wei brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 每從戰伐，恐民有橫被屠戮者，輒以搜簡工匠為言，而全活之。

translations.literal: Whenever following campaigns, fearing the people might be indiscriminately slaughtered, he always spoke of searching out and tallying craftsmen, thereby saving lives.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he often pleaded to register craftsmen and thereby spared many from massacre.

sentences.zh: 歲庚子，卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the year gengzi he died, age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1240 at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，贈中奉大夫、武備院使、神川郡公，諡忠惠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida he was posthumously gifted Middle Maintainer of the Faith, Commissioner of the Armory Court, Duke of Shenchuan, temple name Zhonghui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1309 he was posthumously made Middle Maintainer of the Faith, Armory commissioner, Duke of Shenchuan, with the name Loyal Kindness.

sentences.zh: 子拱，為監察御史，後襲順天安平懷州河南等路甲匠都總管。

translations.literal: His son Gong became investigating censor and later inherited the post of Grand Director-General of armorers for Shuntian, Anping, Huaizhou, Henan, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gong became investigating censor and later inherited the armorers’ directorship for those circuits.

sentences.zh: 巧思如其父，嘗制甲二百八十襲以獻。

translations.literal: Ingenious craft like his father; once he made two hundred eighty suits of armor to present.
translations.idiomatic: He was as ingenious as his father and once presented two hundred eighty suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，別制疊盾，其制，張則為盾，斂則合而易持。

translations.literal: In the 11th year of Zhiyuan he separately made folding shields; the design—expanded they are shields, folded they join and are easy to hold.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274 he devised folding shields that opened into shields and folded for easy carrying.

sentences.zh: 世祖以為古所未有，賜以幣帛。

translations.literal: Shizu regarded them as never before in antiquity and bestowed silks and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai called them unprecedented and rewarded him with silks.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏南征，以甲胄不足，詔諸路集匠民分制。

translations.literal: Chancellor Bayan on the southern campaign, because armor was insufficient, ordered each circuit to gather artisan households to divide production.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan’s southern campaign lacked armor, each circuit was ordered to gather craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 拱董順天、河間甲匠，先期畢工，且象虎豹異獸之形，各殊其制，皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Gong supervised Shuntian and Hejian armorers, completed the work ahead of schedule, and moreover shaped tiger, leopard, and exotic beast forms, each with a different design—all accorded with intent.
translations.idiomatic: Gong oversaw Shuntian and Hejian armorers, finished early, and shaped tiger, leopard, and other beast forms to imperial satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授保定路治中。

translations.literal: In the 15th year he was appointed Administrator of Baoding Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 he was made administrator of Baoding Circuit.

sentences.zh: 適歲饑，議開倉賑民，或曰：「宜請於朝。

translations.literal: It happened to be a famine year; they deliberated opening granaries to relieve the people; some said: "It is fitting to request from court."
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year some urged requesting court permission before opening granaries.

sentences.zh: 」拱曰：「救荒事不可緩也，若得請而後發粟以賑之，則民餒死矣。

translations.literal: Gong said: "Famine relief cannot be delayed; if we must request and then issue grain to relieve, the people will starve to death."
translations.idiomatic: Gong said famine relief could not wait for court approval or people would starve.

sentences.zh: 苟見罪，吾自任之。

translations.literal: If we see punishment, I myself will bear it.
translations.idiomatic: He said he would bear any punishment himself.

sentences.zh: 」遂發粟四千五百石以賑饑民。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued four thousand five hundred shi of grain to relieve the starving people.
translations.idiomatic: He issued four thousand five hundred shi of grain to feed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 高陽土豪據沙河橋取行者錢，人以為病，拱執而罪之。

translations.literal: A Gaoyang strongman held the Shahe Bridge and took travelers’ money—people regarded it as a plague; Gong arrested and punished him.
translations.idiomatic: He arrested a Gaoyang strongman who extorted travelers at Shahe Bridge.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，除武備少卿，遷大都路軍器人匠總管，升工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the 22nd year he was removed as Vice Commissioner of the Armory Court, transferred to Grand Director of Armorer-Artisans of Dadu Circuit, and promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1285 he became vice armory commissioner, then grand director of Dadu armorers, then vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，典朝會供給，賜銀百兩、織紋段五十匹、帛二十五匹、鈔萬貫。

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne he managed court assembly supplies and was bestowed one hundred taels of silver, fifty bolts of brocade, twenty-five bolts of silk, and ten thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: At Chengzong’s accession he managed court supplies and received silver, brocade, silk, and ten thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 元貞二年，授大同路總管，兼府尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanzhen he was appointed Grand Administrator of Datong Circuit, concurrently Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In 1296 he became grand administrator and prefect of Datong.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，遷兩浙都轉運使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade he was transferred to Grand Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1301 he became salt transport commissioner for the Two Zhe.

sentences.zh: 鹽課舊二十五萬引，歲不能足，拱至增五萬引，遂為定額。

translations.literal: The salt quota was formerly two hundred fifty thousand yin per year and could not be filled; when Gong arrived he increased fifty thousand yin and it became the fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: The salt quota of two hundred fifty thousand yin had fallen short until he added fifty thousand and fixed the quota.

sentences.zh: 九年，改益都路總管，兼府尹，仍出內府弓矢寶刀賜之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was changed to Grand Administrator of Yidu Circuit, concurrently Prefect, and again imperial bows, arrows, and treasured blades from the inner storehouse were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1305 he became grand administrator of Yidu with imperial bows and treasured blades from the palace stores.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈大司農、神川郡公，諡文莊。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted Grand Minister of Agriculture, Duke of Shenchuan, temple name Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Minister of Agriculture, Duke of Shenchuan, with the name Cultivated Elegance.

sentences.zh: 阿老瓦丁，回回氏，西域木發里人也。

translations.literal: Ala al-Din, of Huihui stock, a man of Mawar al-Nahr in the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Ala al-Din, a Muslim from Mawar al-Nahr in Central Asia.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，世祖遣使砲匠於宗王阿不哥，王以阿老瓦丁、亦思馬因應詔，二人舉家馳驛至京師，給以官舍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan, Shizu sent envoys to seek artillerists from Prince Abagha; the prince offered Ala al-Din and Ismail; the two brought their families post-haste to the capital and were given official residences.
translations.idiomatic: In 1271 Kublai sought gunners from Prince Abagha, who sent Ala al-Din and Ismail; both families hurried to the capital and received official quarters.

sentences.zh: 首造大砲豎於五門前，帝命試之，各賜衣段。

translations.literal: First they made great cannon erected before the Five Gates; the emperor ordered trials; each was bestowed robes and bolts.
translations.idiomatic: They first built great cannon before the Five Gates; after successful trials each received robes and silk.

sentences.zh: 十一年，國兵渡江，平章阿里海牙遣使求砲手匠，命阿老瓦丁往，破潭州、靜江等郡，悉賴其力。

translations.literal: In the 11th year, when the national army crossed the river, Pacification Commissioner Alihaia sent envoys seeking gunner-artisans; Ala al-Din was ordered to go; he broke Tanzhou, Jingjiang, and other prefectures—all relied on his strength.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274, when the army crossed the Yangtze, Alihaia requested gunners; Ala al-Din helped capture Tanzhou, Jingjiang, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授宣武將軍、管軍總管。

translations.literal: In the 15th year he was appointed General Who Proclaims Martiality and Grand Director of Troops.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 he was made General Who Proclaims Martiality and grand troop director.

sentences.zh: 十七年，陛見，賜鈔五千貫。

translations.literal: In the 17th year he had an audience and was bestowed five thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In 1280 he had an audience and received five thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 十八年，命屯田於南京。

translations.literal: In the 18th year he was ordered to garrison and farm at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 he was ordered to establish garrison farms at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，樞密院奉旨，改元帥府為回回砲手軍匠上萬戶府，以阿老瓦丁為副萬戶。

translations.literal: In the 22nd year the Privy Council received an edict changing the Marshal’s Office to the Huihui Gunner-Artisan Commandery of Ten Thousand Households, with Ala al-Din as vice commander of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In 1285 the Privy Council made the marshal’s office the Muslim Gunner-Artisan Command of Ten Thousand Households, with Ala al-Din as vice commander.

sentences.zh: 大德四年告老。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade he reported old age and retired.
translations.idiomatic: In 1300 he retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 子富謀只，襲副萬戶。

translations.literal: His son Fumouzhi inherited the vice commandership.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fumouzhi inherited the vice commandership.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年卒，子馬哈馬沙襲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he died; his son Mahamasha inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1312; his son Mahamasha succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 亦思馬因，回回氏，西域旭烈人也。

translations.literal: Ismail, of Huihui stock, a man of Xulie in the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Ismail, a Muslim from Xulie in Central Asia.

sentences.zh: 善造砲，至元八年與阿老瓦丁至京師。

translations.literal: Skilled at making cannon; in the eighth year of Zhiyuan he came to the capital with Ala al-Din.
translations.idiomatic: A skilled cannon-maker, he reached the capital with Ala al-Din in 1271.

sentences.zh: 十年，從國兵攻襄陽未下，亦思馬因相地勢，置砲於城東南隅，重一百五十斤，機發，聲震天地，所擊無不摧陷，入地七尺。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, following the national army attacking Xiangyang without taking it, Ismail surveyed the terrain and placed cannon at the southeast corner of the city; weight one hundred fifty jin; when the mechanism fired, the sound shook heaven and earth; whatever was struck was not but destroyed and fell in; it entered the ground seven chi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1273, when Xiangyang resisted siege, he placed a one-hundred-fifty-jin cannon on the southeast corner; its thunderous shots demolished walls seven feet into the earth.

sentences.zh: 宋安撫呂文煥懼，以城降。

translations.literal: Song Pacification Commissioner Lü Wenhuan was afraid and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Song commander Lü Wenhuan surrendered in fear.

sentences.zh: 既而以功賜銀二百五十兩，命為回回砲手總管，佩虎符。

translations.literal: Thereafter for merit he was bestowed two hundred fifty taels of silver and appointed Grand Director of Huihui Gunners, wearing a tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat he received two hundred fifty taels of silver and was made grand director of Muslim gunners with a tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the 11th year he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in 1274.

sentences.zh: 子佈伯襲職。

translations.literal: His son Bubu inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bubu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 時國兵渡江，宋兵陳於南岸，擁舟師迎戰，布伯於北岸豎砲以擊之，舟悉沉沒。

translations.literal: At the time the national army crossed the river; Song troops arrayed on the south bank, mustering boat forces to meet battle; Bubu erected cannon on the north bank to strike them—the boats all sank.
translations.idiomatic: When the army crossed the Yangtze, Song forces massed on the south bank; Bubu sank their fleet with shore batteries.

sentences.zh: 後每戰用之，皆有功。

translations.literal: Afterward whenever battle used them, all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter his cannon proved decisive in battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 十八年，佩三珠虎符，加鎮國上將軍、回回砲手都元帥。

translations.literal: In the 18th year he wore the three-pearl tiger tally and was added Pacifying State General-in-Chief and Grand Marshal of Huihui Gunners.
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 he received the three-pearl tiger tally and was made Pacifying State General-in-Chief and grand marshal of Muslim gunners.

sentences.zh: 明年，改軍匠萬戶府萬戶。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to commander of ten thousand of the Artisan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became commander of the artisan commandery.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，以弟亦不剌金為萬戶，佩元降虎符，官廣威將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Punishments; his younger brother Aibulajin was made commander of ten thousand, wearing the tally of the original surrender, office General of Expansive Might.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of punishments; his brother Aibulajin became commander with the original surrender tally as General of Expansive Might.

sentences.zh: 布伯俄進通奉大夫、浙東道宣慰使，賜鈔二萬五千貫，俾養老焉。

translations.literal: Bubu soon was advanced to Grand Master for Attending to Governance and Pacification Commissioner of Zhedong Circuit, bestowed twenty-five thousand strings of paper money, and enabled to retire in comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Bubu was soon promoted to grand master and Zhedong pacification commissioner with twenty-five thousand strings for retirement.

sentences.zh: 子哈散，廕授昭信校尉、高郵府同知。

translations.literal: His son Hasan was yin-appointed Colonel of Manifest Trust and Vice Administrator of Gaoyou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hasan inherited appointment as vice prefect of Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 致和元年八月，樞密院檄亦不剌金所部軍匠至京師，賜鈔二千五百貫、金綺四端，與馬哈馬沙造砲。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Zhihe, the Privy Council ordered Aibulajin’s artisan troops to the capital and bestowed two thousand five hundred strings, four bolts of gold brocade, to make cannon with Mahamasha.
translations.idiomatic: In August 1328 the Privy Council summoned Aibulajin’s artisans to the capital with funds to build cannon with Mahamasha.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansli he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1329.

sentences.zh: 子亞古襲。

translations.literal: His son Yagu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yagu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 阿尼哥，尼波羅國人也，其國人稱之曰八魯布。

translations.literal: Anige, a man of Nepal; his countrymen called him Arub.
translations.idiomatic: Anige of Nepal was known in his homeland as Arub.

sentences.zh: 幼敏悟異凡兒，稍長，誦習佛書，期年能曉其義。

translations.literal: In youth keen and perceptive beyond ordinary children; when slightly grown he recited and studied Buddhist books; in one year he could understand their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was unusually quick; within a year of studying Buddhist texts he understood their meaning.

sentences.zh: 同學有為繪畫妝塑業者，讀《尺寸經》，阿尼哥一聞，即能記​​。

translations.literal: A fellow student practiced the crafts of painting and clay sculpture; reading the Classic of Measurements, Anige upon one hearing could remember.
translations.idiomatic: When a classmate read the Classic of Measurements for painting and sculpture, Anige memorized it at once.

sentences.zh: 長善畫塑，及鑄金為像。

translations.literal: Grown, he excelled at painting and sculpture and casting gold into images.
translations.idiomatic: He grew adept at painting, sculpture, and casting gold images.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，命帝師八合斯巴建黃金塔於吐蕃，尼波羅國選匠百人往成之，得八十人，求部送之人未得。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, Imperial Preceptor Phagspa was ordered to build a golden pagoda in Tibet; Nepal selected a hundred craftsmen to complete it and obtained eighty; one to head and escort them was not obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In 1260 Phagspa was ordered to build a golden pagoda in Tibet; Nepal sent eighty craftsmen but lacked a leader.

sentences.zh: 阿尼哥年十七，請行，眾以其幼，難之。

translations.literal: Anige was seventeen and requested to go; everyone because of his youth found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen-year-old Anige volunteered, though many doubted his youth.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「年幼心不幼也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Though young in years, the heart is not young."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I may be young in years, but not in resolve."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent.

sentences.zh: 帝師一見奇之，命監其役。

translations.literal: The Imperial Preceptor upon one meeting found him extraordinary and ordered him to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: Phagspa took him for remarkable and put him in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 明年，塔成，請歸，帝師勉以入朝，乃祝髮受具為弟子，從帝師入見。

translations.literal: The next year the pagoda was completed; he requested return; the Imperial Preceptor urged him to enter court; thereupon he tonsured and received full ordination as disciple, following the Imperial Preceptor to audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the pagoda was finished the next year, Phagspa urged him to court; he tonsured, became Phagspa’s disciple, and entered audience.

sentences.zh: 帝視之久，問曰：「汝來大國，得無懼乎？

translations.literal: The emperor gazed long and asked: "You come to the great state—are you not afraid?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor studied him and asked whether he feared coming to the great empire.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「聖人子育萬方，子至父前，何懼之有。

translations.literal: He replied: "The sage nourishes the ten thousand regions; a son coming before his father—what fear is there?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered that the Son of Heaven nourished all under Heaven, and a son before his father had nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」又問：「汝來何為？

translations.literal: Again asked: "For what do you come?"
translations.idiomatic: Asked why he had come,

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣家西域，奉命造塔吐蕃，二載而成。

translations.literal: He replied: "My family is in the Western Regions; I received command to build a pagoda in Tibet; in two years it was completed."
translations.idiomatic: he said his family was in the west and he had built the Tibetan pagoda in two years.

sentences.zh: 見彼土兵難，民不堪命，願陛下安輯之，不遠萬里，為生靈而來耳。

translations.literal: Seeing that land’s military hardship and the people unable to bear commands, he wished Your Majesty to pacify them—not ten thousand li distant, but for living souls he came.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Tibet ravaged by war and the people suffering, he had come to beg the emperor to pacify them—not for gain but for the people.

sentences.zh: 」又問：「汝何所能？

translations.literal: Again asked: "What can you do?"
translations.idiomatic: Asked what he could do,

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣以心為師，頗知畫塑鑄金之藝。

translations.literal: He replied: "I take the heart as teacher and am fairly knowledgeable in the arts of painting, sculpture, and casting gold."
translations.idiomatic: he said he took the heart as teacher and knew painting, sculpture, and metal casting.

sentences.zh: 」帝命取明堂針灸銅像示之曰：「此宣撫王楫使宋時所進，歲久闕壞，無能修完之者，汝能新之乎？

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Bright Hall acupuncture bronze figure brought forth and shown, saying: "This was presented when Pacification Commissioner Wang Ji went to Song; years long damaged—none can repair it complete—can you renew it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed the damaged Song bronze acupuncture figure Wang Ji had once presented and asked whether he could restore it.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣雖未嘗為此，請試之。

translations.literal: He replied: "Though I have never done this, I request to try."
translations.idiomatic: He said he had never done so but would try.

sentences.zh: 」至元二年，新像成，關鬲脈絡皆備，金工歎其天巧，莫不愧服。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan the new figure was completed; joints and channels all complete; metalworkers sighed at its heaven-sent skill—all ashamed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1265 the new figure was finished with every joint and channel perfect, astonishing the metalworkers.

sentences.zh: 凡兩京寺觀之像，多出其手。

translations.literal: Generally images of temples and monasteries in the two capitals mostly came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Most temple images in both capitals were his work.

sentences.zh: 為七寶鑌鐵法輪，車駕行幸，用以前導。

translations.literal: He made a seven-jewel wrought-iron dharma wheel used when the imperial carriage traveled in procession as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He made a seven-jewel iron dharma wheel that led the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 原廟列聖御容，織錦為之，圖畫弗及也。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple’s portraits of successive sages in imperial likeness were woven in brocade—painting could not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral portraits at the temple were woven in brocade beyond what painting could achieve.

sentences.zh: 至元十年，始授人匠總管，銀章虎符。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan he was first appointed Grand Director of Artisans, silver seal and tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In 1273 he was first made Grand Director of Artisans with silver seal and tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 十五年，有詔返初服，授光祿大夫，大司徒，領將作院事，寵遇賞賜，無與為比。

translations.literal: In the 15th year there was an edict returning him to secular dress; he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Minister of Education, in charge of the Directorate of Palace Construction—favor and rewards none could compare.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 he was restored to lay dress and made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Minister of Education heading palace construction, with unmatched favor.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太師、開府儀同三司、涼國公、上柱國，諡敏慧。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously gifted Grand Preceptor, Opening the Government with Equal Ceremony to the Three Ducal Ministers, Duke of Liang, Senior Pillar of State, temple name Minhui.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously ennobled Duke of Liang with the name Keen Wisdom and the highest honors.

sentences.zh: 子六人，曰阿僧哥，大司徒；

translations.literal: Six sons: one called Asungge, Grand Minister of Education;
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons, including Asungge, Grand Minister of Education,

sentences.zh: 阿述臘，諸色人匠總管府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Ashula, Darughachi of the Grand Directorate of Artisans of All Categories.
translations.idiomatic: and Ashula, darughachi of the artisans directorate.

sentences.zh: 有劉元者，嘗從阿尼哥學西天梵相，亦稱絕藝。

translations.literal: There was one Liu Yuan who once studied Western Heaven Brahma images under Anige—also styled unsurpassed craft.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan studied Western Buddhist sculpture under Anige and was also deemed a master.

sentences.zh: 元字秉元，薊之寶坻人。

translations.literal: Yuan’s style name was Bingyuan, a man of Baodi in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan (Bingyuan) was from Baodi in Ji.

sentences.zh: 始為黃冠，師事青州把道錄，傳其藝非一。

translations.literal: At first he was a Daoist priest, studying under the Qingzhou abbot Ba Daolu, transmitting more than one of his crafts.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Daoist under Abbot Ba of Qingzhou and learned many arts from him.

sentences.zh: 至元中，凡兩都名剎，塑土、范金、搏換為佛像，出元手者，神思妙合，天下稱之。

translations.literal: In the Zhiyuan period, famous monasteries in both capitals—clay, cast gold, and boluan Buddha images from Yuan’s hand—all had spirit and wonderful union; the realm acclaimed them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kublai, clay, gilt, and boluan Buddha images at famous temples in both capitals from his hand won universal acclaim.

sentences.zh: 其上都三皇尤古粹，識者以為造意得三聖人之微者。

translations.literal: His Three Sovereigns at Shangdu were especially ancient and pure; connoisseurs held that in creative intent he grasped the subtlety of the three sages.
translations.idiomatic: His Three Sovereigns at Shangdu were especially revered as capturing the essence of the ancient sages.

sentences.zh: 由是兩賜宮女為妻，命以官長其屬，行幸必從。

translations.literal: Thereupon twice palace women were bestowed as wives; he was ordered to head his subordinates; on imperial journeys he must follow.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice given palace women as wives, made head of his craft, and always accompanied the emperor on journeys.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘗敕元非有旨不許為人造他神像。

translations.literal: Renzong once commanded Yuan that without an edict he was not permitted to make other-god images for people.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong forbade him to make images of other deities for private patrons without an edict.

sentences.zh: 後大都南城作東嶽廟，元為造仁聖帝像，巍巍然有帝王之度，其侍臣像，乃若憂深思遠者。

translations.literal: Later the Eastern Peak Temple was built in the southern city of Dadu; Yuan made the image of the Sage Emperor of Benevolence—towering with an emperor’s bearing; his attendant images were as if worried and thinking far.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sculpted the Lord of Mount Tai at Dadu’s new Eastern Peak Temple with imperial majesty and attendants deep in thought.

sentences.zh: 始元欲作侍臣像，久之未措手，適閱秘書圖畫，見唐魏徵像，矍然曰：「得之矣，非若此，莫稱為相臣者。

translations.literal: At first Yuan wished to make attendant images; long he did not set hand; happening to read secretariat pictures, he saw Tang Wei Zheng’s image, started awake and said: "Got it—if not like this, one cannot be called a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Long hesitant over attendant figures, he found his model in a Tang portrait of Wei Zheng and cried that only such a face could stand for a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 」遽走廟中為之，即日成，士大夫觀者，咸嘆異焉。

translations.literal: He immediately ran to the temple to make it; that day it was completed; gentlemen and officials viewing all sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: He finished the attendant that same day to the wonder of all who viewed it.

sentences.zh: 其所為西番佛像多秘，人罕得見者。

translations.literal: His Western Tibet Buddha images were mostly secret—people rarely could see them.
translations.idiomatic: His Tibetan Buddhist images were mostly kept secret and rarely seen.

sentences.zh: 元官為昭文館大學士、正奉大夫、秘書卿，以壽終。

translations.literal: Yuan’s office was Grand Academician of the Hall for the Glorification of Culture, Grand Master for Attending to Governance, Secretary Director—he ended by longevity.
translations.idiomatic: He served as grand academician, grand master, and secretary director and died at an advanced age.

sentences.zh: 搏換者，漫帛土偶上而髹之，已而去其土，髹帛儼然成像云。

translations.literal: Boluan means: spread silk over a clay figurine and lacquer it; afterward remove the clay—the lacquered silk stands complete as an image.
translations.idiomatic: Boluan is the technique of lacquering silk over a clay core and removing the clay, leaving a hollow lacquered image.
